summary.text: Marcus Riccelli, a Democrat from Spokane, represents the 3rd Legislative District in the Washington State Senate after 12 years in the House. His official biography says he was elected to the Senate in 2024 and serves as Majority Floor Leader.

paragraphs.text: Riccelli was born and raised in Spokane and graduated from Gonzaga University with a bachelor's in business administration and from the University of Washington with a master's in public administration, according to his official biography.

It says that from 2007 to 2010 he served as U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell's Eastern Washington Director and from 2010 to 2012 as Senior Policy Advisor to Washington State Senate Majority Leader Lisa Brown.
The page says he was elected to the state legislature in 2012, served 12 years in the House and was elected to the Senate in 2024.
As Majority Floor Leader he also serves on the Ways & Means, Health & Long-Term Care, State Government, Tribal Affairs & Elections, and Rules committees, according to the page.
Outside the legislature, the page says Riccelli is a Community Relations Manager for CHAS Health and has been an adjunct instructor at Eastern Washington University.
It credits him as prime sponsor of legislation creating the WSU Elson S. Floyd College of Medicine and says he lives in Spokane with his wife, Amanda, and their two children.
